papers.title: PERAN GURU DALAM MENINGKATKAN MOTIVASI BELAJAR SISWA STUDI LITARATUR
papers.abstract: Declining mental engagement among students in the classroom often stems from how teachers design learning experiences, yet prior studies tend to examine instructional factors and environmental support in isolation. Addressing this conceptual gap, this article aims to re-examine the multidimensional role of educators in fostering student learning motivation through an in-depth literature review. Employing a qualitative approach with a narrative literature review design, literature searches were conducted across five academic databases for publications spanning 2022–2025. Staged screening following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) protocol filtered 482 initial records down to 30 peer-reviewed journal articles as the final sample. Data were recorded via a data extraction sheet and processed using thematic-descriptive analysis. Thematic mapping yielded eight focus clusters integrated into five core dimensions of teacher roles: pedagogical and professional competence balancing classroom structure with autonomy, empathetic interpersonal communication, active learning strategies supported by digital media, effort-based positive reinforcement, and environmental management alongside family synergy. The systemic synergy of these five dimensions serves as a motivational ecosystem driver that fosters extrinsic drive while sustaining students’ intrinsic learning awareness. ABSTRAK Melemahnya keterlibatan mental peserta didik di ruang kelas sering kali berakar pada cara guru merancang pengalaman belajar, namun kajian terdahulu cenderung membedah faktor pengajaran dan dukungan lingkungan secara terpisah. Menjawab celah konseptual tersebut, artikel ini bertujuan menelaah kembali peran multidimensi pendidik dalam menumbuhkan semangat belajar siswa melalui penelusuran pustaka secara mendalam. Menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan rancangan narrative literature review, penelusuran literatur dilakukan pada lima pangkalan data akademik untuk publikasi periode 2022–2025. Seleksi bertahap berdasarkan protokol Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) menyaring 482 rekaman awal hingga menetapkan 30 artikel jurnal ilmiah sebagai sampel akhir. Data direkam melalui data extraction sheet dan diolah menggunakan analisis tematik-deskriptif. Pemetaan temuan menghasilkan delapan klaster fokus kajian yang terintegrasi ke dalam lima dimensi utama peran guru, meliputi kompetensi pedagogik dan profesional yang menyeimbangkan struktur kelas serta otonomi, komunikasi interpersonal empatik, strategi belajar aktif berbantuan media digital, penguatan berbasis proses usaha, serta pengelolaan lingkungan dan sinergi keluarga. Sinergi sistemik kelima dimensi tersebut terbukti menjadi penggerak ekosistem motivasi yang menumbuhkan dorongan ekstrinsik sekaligus merawat kesadaran belajar intrinsik siswa secara berkelanjutan.

papers.title: Preoperative optimisation before revision total hip arthroplasty: a systematic review of modifiable risk factors and optimisation strategies
papers.abstract: Introduction Revision total hip arthroplasty (rTHA) is associated with perioperative morbidity and healthcare utilisation. Preoperative optimisation may improve outcomes, but revision-specific evidence remains poorly defined. Objective To evaluate preoperative factors and optimisation strategies associated with rTHA outcomes and identify areas where evidence for active intervention remains lacking. Methods PubMed, MEDLINE and Embase were searched from inception to September 2026 for primary studies evaluating preoperative optimisation, modifiable risk factors or related interventions in adults undergoing rTHA. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and PROBAST principles. Owing to clinical and methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesised narratively. Results The search identified 226 records; 103 remained after 123 duplicates were removed, and 15 studies were included. No randomised controlled trials were identified. Anaemia was the most consistently investigated potentially modifiable factor and was associated with transfusion, complications, prolonged length of stay and readmission. Hypoalbuminaemia, chronic opioid exposure, depression, obesity, impaired functional status, renal dysfunction, liver disease and cardiopulmonary comorbidity also identified higher-risk patients. An opioid-free interval was associated with attenuation of excess risk in one observational study. Fast-track pathways reduced length of stay, although readmission remained high. No eligible study directly investigated structured preoperative physiotherapy or exercise-based prehabilitation specifically before rTHA. Conclusion Multiple potentially modifiable preoperative factors are associated with adverse outcomes following rTHA, with anaemia demonstrating the most consistent revision-specific evidence. However, current literature is predominantly retrospective and prognostic, and evidence that active correction of identified risks improves outcomes remains limited. Prospective interventional studies, particularly of multimodal optimisation and exercise-based prehabilitation, are required.

N. Cooper Municipal General Hospital, Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. ³Senior Resident, Grant Government Medical College and Sir J. J. Group of Hospitals, Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. Corresponding Author: Dr. Karan Keshav Malave, Senior Resident, Lokmanya Tilak Municipal Medical College and General Hospital, Sion, Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24387380 Received: 07 October 2026, Revised: 22 October 2026, Accepted: 07 November 2026, Online First: 22 November 2026 ABSTRACT Background: Displaced intracapsular fractures of the femoral neck in older adults represent a high-burden injury associated with significant mortality risk, prolonged disability, and loss of independent ambulation. Bipolar hemiarthroplasty remains widely adopted in many low- and middle-income settings because it offers predictable pain relief and functional restoration with lower cost and shorter operative time than total hip arthroplasty (THA). However, fixation choice for the femoral stem cemented versus uncemented remains controversial. Cemented stems may provide superior immediate stability in osteoporotic bone and potentially faster early recovery, but carry risk of peri‑cementation hemodynamic instability consistent with bone cement implantation syndrome (BCIS). Objectives: To compare perioperative safety and short-term clinical and functional outcomes of cemented versus uncemented bipolar hemiarthroplasty in adults older than 55 years with displaced femoral neck fractures, with emphasis on intraoperative blood pressure (BP) fall, early surgical site infection (SSI), pain, and functional recovery. Methods: A prospective observational study was conducted over 18 months (January 2023 to June 2024). Forty‑one patients aged >55 years with displaced femoral neck fractures underwent bipolar hemiarthroplasty via a standardized posterior approach. Cemented fixation was performed in 23 patients and uncemented fixation in 18. Outcomes included intraoperative BP fall (none, 5–10 mmHg, >10 mmHg), Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) pain at 6 weeks, SSI before suture removal, and Harris Hip Score (HHS) at 6 weeks, 3 months, and 6 months. Secondary functional indicators included limb length discrepancy (LLD), limp, ambulation status, walking distance, stair climbing, nail trimming ability, public transportation use, and sitting tolerance. Results: Baseline characteristics were similar between groups. Intraoperative BP fall differed significantly (p<0.001): “no fall” occurred in 1/23 cemented cases versus 15/18 uncemented cases; BP fall 5–10 mmHg occurred in 19/23 cemented versus 3/18 uncemented; BP fall >10 mmHg occurred in 3/23 cemented versus 0 uncemented. VAS pain at 6 weeks was similar (4.22±2.55 vs 5.06±2.15; p=0.272). SSI rates were comparable (2/23 vs 2/18; p=0.796). HHS did not differ significantly at 6 weeks (p=0.096), 3 months (p=0.356), or 6 months (p=0.169). LLD pattern differed (p=0.008), while most mobility indicators were broadly comparable. Conclusion: Cemented and uncemented bipolar hemiarthroplasty provided comparable short‑term functional outcomes up to 6 months. Cemented fixation was associated with markedly higher frequency of intraoperative BP fall, reinforcing the need for systematic BCIS‑aware anesthetic vigilance and cementation safety protocols. Keywords: femoral neck fracture; bipolar hemiarthroplasty; cemented; uncemented; Harris Hip Score; bone cement implantation syndrome; older adults; India INTRODUCTION Hip fracture is a sentinel injury in geriatric trauma and an increasingly important public health challenge. Beyond the immediate surgical episode, hip fractures often precipitate sustained declines in mobility and independence, increase caregiver dependence, and impose substantial costs on families and healthcare systems. Epidemiologic projections indicate that global hip fracture incidence will continue to rise sharply due to population aging and increased prevalence of osteoporosis and frailty, with a growing proportion occurring in Asia, including India (1,2). These trends have major implications for orthopaedic services, perioperative medicine, rehabilitation capacity, and long-term care infrastructure. Outcomes after hip fracture are shaped by both injury biology and the physiology of frailty. Older adults commonly present with multimorbidity, sarcopenia, cognitive vulnerability, and limited cardiopulmonary reserve. Consequently, immobility-related complications delirium, pneumonia, venous thromboembolism, pressure injuries, and functional deconditioning—represent major drivers of morbidity. Modern care models therefore emphasize timely surgery after optimization, coordinated multidisciplinary perioperative care, and early mobilization with a goal of immediate weight bearing where feasible. NICE guidance on hip fracture management highlights operating with the aim of allowing patients to fully weight bear without restriction immediately postoperatively and emphasizes consistent perioperative pathways and implant strategy (3). The American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons (AAOS) similarly provides evidence-based recommendations for the management of hip fractures in older adults, with emphasis on coordinated care and appropriate procedure selection (4). Displaced intracapsular femoral neck fractures constitute a clinically distinct subset. Their intracapsular location disrupts femoral head blood supply and places union at risk, especially in osteoporotic bone. In older adults, internal fixation of displaced intracapsular fractures carries substantial risk of non‑union, avascular necrosis, and reoperation. As a result, replacement arthroplasty hemiarthroplasty or total hip arthroplasty (THA) is commonly recommended for many older patients with displaced intracapsular fractures. THA may offer superior functional outcomes in carefully selected, independently mobile patients; however, hemiarthroplasty remains widely used because it generally requires less operative time, is technically less demanding, and may have a lower dislocation risk in frail populations. In many tertiary care centers in India and other low- and middle-income settings, bipolar hemiarthroplasty remains a pragmatic and common option. Bipolar designs were developed to allow movement at an inner articulation, theoretically reducing acetabular wear and pain compared with unipolar constructs while remaining less resource‑intensive than THA. Even though acetabular erosion can still occur and some patients may later require conversion to THA, bipolar hemiarthroplasty provides reliable early pain relief and functional restoration for many older, low-demand patients. A central technical decision in hemiarthroplasty is the method of femoral stem fixation: cemented versus uncemented (cementless). Cemented fixation provides immediate mechanical stability, potentially improving early mobility and reducing postoperative thigh pain, particularly in osteoporotic bone. Multiple randomized trials and meta‑analyses report modest functional advantages and reduced mechanical complications such as periprosthetic fracture with cemented stems compared with uncemented stems (5–8). A major contemporary randomized trial found cemented hemiarthroplasty produced modestly better quality of life and lower periprosthetic fracture risk than uncemented fixation for intracapsular hip fracture (9). Conversely, uncemented fixation avoids cement-related physiological effects and may shorten operative time in some settings, but can be challenging in osteoporotic femora where press‑fit fixation is less reliable and may increase risk of mechanical complications (5–8). Cementation introduces unique physiological risk. Bone cement implantation syndrome (BCIS) refers to a spectrum of peri‑cementation events including hypoxia, hypotension, arrhythmia, and in severe cases cardiovascular collapse. BCIS is particularly relevant to hip fracture surgery because patients are often elderly, frail, and comorbid (10). Professional safety guidance has therefore emphasized structured mitigation: preoperative risk stratification, enhanced monitoring, high inspired oxygen at cementation, adequate intravascular volume, clear team communication at cementation, and readiness for prompt vasopressor support (11). Within this context, prospective local data are valuable because outcomes depend not only on implant design but also on patient profile, anesthetic resources, rehabilitation intensity, and institutional protocols. The present prospective observational study therefore compared cemented versus uncemented bipolar hemiarthroplasty in adults older than 55 years with displaced femoral neck fractures at a tertiary care center in India, with emphasis on perioperative hemodynamics and short-term functional outcomes up to 6 months. To compare functional outcomes after uncemented bipolar hemiarthroplasty for displaced femoral neck fracture in older adults. 3. To compare perioperative complications and early outcomes, with emphasis on intraoperative BP fall, SSI before suture removal, postoperative pain, and mobility-related functional indicators. papers.title: Parametric Non‐Intrusive Reduced Order Modelling via Taylor Series Neural Networks and Dynamic Identification
papers.abstract: Numerically solving parameterised partial differential equations (P‐PDEs) is both valuable and computationally intensive, driving the development of reduced‐order models (ROMs). Recently, methods that combine latent space identification techniques with deep learning algorithms (e.g., autoencoders) have shown great potential in describing the dynamical system in the lower‐dimensional latent space. In this paper, a new parametric latent identification of nonlinear dynamics neural networks, P‐TLDINets, is introduced, which relies on a novel neural network structure based on Taylor series expansion and ResNets to learn the parametric differential equations that govern the dynamics in the latent space. During the training process, Taylor series‐based Latent Dynamic Neural Network (TLDNet) and identified equations are trained simultaneously to generate a smoother latent space. In order to facilitate the parameterised study, a ‐nearest neighbours (KNN) method based on an inverse distance weighting (IDW) interpolation scheme is introduced to predict the identified ODE coefficients using local information. Compared to other latent dynamics identification methods based on autoencoders, P‐TLDINet eliminates the encoder‐decoder's dependence on spatial coordinates, enabling it to be a parameterised ROM. Additionally, its lightweight network structure allows high generalization capabilities with less training time. P‐TLDINet was tested on the 2D Burgers' equation and the lock‐exchange case, maintaining an error of less than 2% compared to high‐fidelity models.

papers.title: THE 2026 BRUCE SMITH SR. AWARD ADDRESS: Enhancing Our Mission to Deliver a Superior Educational Experience: Four Strategies
papers.abstract: The Academy of Criminal Justice Sciences is a professional organization whose mission is to promote education, research, and practice within the discipline of criminal justice. Its implicit purpose is to educate the next generation of practitioners, academics and policy analysts/decision-makers to advance the discipline and develop skill sets to promote democratic social control. This paper explores four strategies designed to do this in an educational environment. The four strategies discussed are: 1) Demonstrate relevance of criminal justice topics covered in a course that relate directly to the understanding of the justice system and its potential improvement; 2) Encourage classroom engagement through the use of active learning techniques; 3) Ensure involvement in the actual practices of the criminal justice system; and 4) Create a congenial learning environment. The paper concludes by discussing how the students’ educational experience can be evaluated and continually improved to generate the next generation of thoughtful and educated field professionals, academics/researchers and policy analysts/decision-makers.

papers.title: Enforcing continuous symmetry in physics-informed neural networks for solving the 1D wave equation
papers.abstract: As a typical application of deep learning, Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN) have gained significant attention in recent years as a mesh-free framework for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) under the paradigm of artificial intelligence for Science. However, improving their limited accuracy remains a major challenge for PINN. Symmetry-enhanced Physics-Informed Neural Networks (SPINN) embed the invariant surface conditions derived from the Lie symmetries of PDEs into the loss function of PINN, so as to improve the solution accuracy of PDEs. This paper is the first to extend SPINN to solve the 1D wave equation, and conducts a comparative analysis with PINN. Numerical experiments show that SPINN can effectively solve the 1D wave equation. Compared with the PINN method, SPINN demonstrates better performance and effectiveness, with its predictive accuracy improved by one to two orders of magnitude, exhibiting superior predictive precision and generalization capability.

papers.title: Enhanced Finite Control Set‐Based Predictive Torque Control for Maximum Power Extraction in Wind Turbine System
papers.abstract: In large‐scale wind energy conversion systems (WECSs), three‐level neutral point clamped (3L‐NPC) converters, and finite control set model predictive control (FCS‐MPC) schemes are attractive for high‐power operation because of their direct switching control and fast dynamic response. However, the increased number of voltage vectors in the 3L‐NPC converter increases the computational burden of the conventional FCS‐MPC scheme. In addition, most current‐based predictive controllers mainly focus on ()‐axis current tracking, whereas maximum power extraction and stable generator operation are more directly associated with electromagnetic torque and stator flux behavior. To address these issues, this study proposes an enhanced model predictive torque control (EMPTC) strategy for improving the machine‐side converter performance of a 20 MW permanent magnet vernier generator (PMVG)‐based WECS. In the proposed method, a two‐stage prediction structure is used as a computationally efficient switching‐state selection framework. In the first stage, six virtual space vectors are evaluated using predicted machine current information to identify the suitable voltage‐vector region. Then, in the second stage, the final switching state is selected from the corresponding real voltage‐vector candidates using a multi‐objective cost function based on predicted electromagnetic torque, stator flux, and switching frequency. Moreover, capacitor voltage information is used for the conditional selection of small voltage vectors in Stage II, thereby supporting neutral point voltage balancing without its influence in the cost function. The proposed controller is validated in MATLAB/Simulink under step and randomly varying wind speed conditions and compared with existing FCS‐MPC schemes. The comparison results show that the proposed EMPTC improves torque generation, power extraction performance, and steady‐state behavior while reducing the switching‐state evaluation burden for PMVG‐based large‐scale WECS operation.

papers.title: Fixed-Wing versus Multirotor UAV Recognition from Radar Track Kinematics Using a Jump-Markov Multiple-Model Estimator
papers.abstract: Recognising whether a small unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) is of fixed-wing or multirotor type is a prerequisite for threat assessment and countermeasure selection in counter-UAS surveillance, yet many deployed surveillance radars provide only plot-level kinematics without micro-Doppler signatures. Falileev and Shatovkin (2020) proposed recognising the UAV type from track kinematics alone, exploiting the fact that only rotary-wing platforms can hover for a sustained period: a three-mode jump-Markov system (manoeuvre, non-manoeuvre, hover) is estimated with a second-order generalised pseudo-Bayesian (GPB2) filter, and a rotary-wing declaration is issued when the hover mode is estimated on n consecutive scans within the same azimuth sector. This paper restates that algorithm in a reproducible form, analyses its transition probability matrices (TPMs), and evaluates it by Monte Carlo simulation over 1,300 synthetic radar tracks at a 3 s update period. We show that the published TPMs are not row-stochastic and, once normalised, have identical rows, i.e. they describe a memoryless mode process that cannot accumulate evidence over scans. In our simulations the published parameterisation never declared a multirotor (0/600 tracks, measurement noise 1–25 m). Replacing the TPM with a diagonally dominant, persistence-aware matrix yields 100% recognition of multirotors at every noise level with a median latency of 9–12 s after hover onset and at most 1% false declarations on nominal fixed-wing tracks, against a median latency of 6–63 s for a filtered speed-threshold baseline. For low-airspeed fixed-wing aircraft flying into strong headwinds, a horizontal-velocity gate on the mode-conditioned estimate reduces false declarations from 38% to 8% (3-of-3 rule) at a cost of 3 s median latency. We discuss the latency–false-alarm trade-off governed by n and the fundamental limits of kinematics-only recognition.

papers.title: Learning Gaussian Process Priors with Linear Semigroups and Kinetic Regularisation
papers.abstract: We introduce a semigroup-based construction of Gaussian process (GP) priors. A linear semigroup transforms a source GP at $t=0$ into a prior at $t=1$, enabling computationally tractable regression. Linearity preserves Gaussianity, allowing us to characterise the evolution of the covariance and draw connections with optimal transport and convolution models. The semigroup is parametrised by its generator, which is learned through two competing objectives: the marginal likelihood encourages agreement with observations, while a kinetic-energy regulariser favours lower-energy trajectories and limits unnecessary mass displacement from the source GP. Experiments on independent GP draws show that, with sufficiently many training functions, the learned prior provides accurate predictions on held-out functions, while kinetic regularisation substantially reduces the energy of the generated trajectories without compromising prediction accuracy.

papers.title: probly: Uncertainty-Aware Machine Learning
papers.abstract: As machine learning systems are increasingly deployed in real-world applications, the question of how to represent and quantify uncertainty has moved from a methodological side issue to a central concern. In practice, however, making a model uncertainty-aware is still surprisingly difficult: relevant tools tend to be scattered across libraries, each tied to a particular framework and a particular approach to modeling uncertainty, and the choice of representation, quantification, and evaluation is typically left to the user without much guidance. In this paper, we present probly, a Python package that addresses these issues in a single, modular framework. probly offers (i) lightweight transformations that turn existing models into uncertainty-aware ones, currently supporting PyTorch, scikit-learn, and Flax, (ii) several representations, including second-order distributions, credal sets, and conformal prediction, (iii) the corresponding quantification measures, and (iv) a number of evaluation protocols, which can be combined more or less arbitrarily. Using probly, we conduct a benchmark study on three standard tasks --- selective prediction, out-of-distribution detection, and active learning. In addition, and unlike existing benchmarks, we evaluate suitable methods on first-order data, i.e., datasets for which the target itself is a distribution over outcomes. We further illustrate the flexibility of the package on a number of less standard case studies, including large language models, graph neural networks, and data streams. The package is publicly available at https://github.com/pwhofman/probly.

papers.title: CarlHOI: Counterfactual Predictive Imagination for Generalizable Multi-Humanoid Object Interaction under Constrained Environments
papers.abstract: Recent advances in physics-based humanoid control enable teams of varying sizes to coordinate their movements and cooperatively transport shared objects. However, adapting learned cooperative behaviors to unseen environmental constraints remains challenging, particularly when obstacles require coordinated detours and changes in team configuration. We propose CarlHOI, a counterfactual predictive imagination framework built upon a counterfactual-anchored relational latent world model (CarlWM) for human-object interaction (HOI), enabling multi-humanoid teams to adapt to unseen environmental constraints without retraining their underlying cooperative control policies. CarlHOI explicitly represents the shared object, individual humanoids, and environmental obstacles as interacting entities. Trained offline using counterfactual simulator rollouts, the model imagines alternative collective futures under different shared waypoint commands, predicting how the coupled humanoid team and object would respond. By evaluating these imagined outcomes through predicted progress, failure, and contact risks, and long-horizon value estimates, CarlHOI selects adaptive guidance commands while preserving the pretrained cooperative controller. We introduce a benchmark comprising three challenging obstacle-constrained transport tasks to evaluate adaptation and generalization. Despite being trained exclusively with four humanoids, our model generalizes without retraining to teams of two to ten humanoids, unseen obstacle geometries and placements, unseen objects, and novel combinations of environmental constraints. Extensive experiments demonstrate improved cooperative transport success over evaluated baselines across diverse configurations. Results highlight the potential of counterfactual predictive imagination to extend pretrained multi-humanoid cooperative skills beyond their original training conditions.

papers.title: Performance Evaluation of Nonlinear Model Predictive and Sliding Mode Controllers on a 4-Cable Spatial CSPR in Simscape
papers.abstract: This paper offers a comprehensive comparative study between Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) and Sliding Mode Control (SMC) applied to a spatial Cable-Suspended Parallel Robot (CSPR) actuated by four cables. The robot is modeled in two parallel ways: (i) via an analytical dynamic model with included cable elasticity and frictional losses, and (ii) in MATLAB Simscape Multibody, capturing realistic physical effects. Both controllers are implemented under identical reference trajectories, system constraints, and tuning strategies. Our results show that NMPC achieves superior tracking accuracy and stronger disturbance rejection compared to SMC, but at the cost of higher computational demand. Moreover, both controllers were tested on an analytical model of the robot and a Simscape model. The close agreement between the two, for both control schemes, confirms the accuracy of the analytical formulation and its consistency with the physics-based simulation. The study highlights the value of physics-based simulation as a complementary tool for validating advanced controllers under realistic conditions, and demonstrates that NMPC offers superior performance for the studied high-precision, constrained CSPR.

papers.title: Grounded in Contact: Reducing Floating and Interpenetration Artifacts with Multimodal Skill-Effect Models
papers.abstract: Learning to predict the effects of contact-rich manipulation skills requires models that represent distinct outcome modes rather than a single expected result. Even for basic skills such as pushing, picking, and placing, small variations in contact conditions or object geometry can produce qualitatively different object motions under nearly identical states and actions. Deterministic and Gaussian models tend to average over these alternatives or represent them as a single broad distribution, obscuring distinct modes such as sliding, toppling, and rotating. We study probabilistic skill-effect models that learn multimodal distributions over object pose changes given partial point clouds and actions. We instantiate this abstraction with three representative model classes: mixture density networks, state tokenization, and flow matching, each paired with latent dynamics for next-step prediction. Across diverse objects and skills, explicitly multimodal models predict which outcome occurs more accurately than deterministic and Gaussian baselines. In planning, flow matching significantly improves task success over the deterministic baseline on every skill and achieves the highest success on every multi-step sequence. On a real robot, probabilistic models succeed at pick about twice as often as the deterministic baseline, providing evidence that probabilistic skill effects offer a practical abstraction for reasoning and planning under uncertainty.

papers.title: GravHMR: Coupling SLAM and Human Mesh Recovery in a Shared Gravity Frame
papers.abstract: Recovering globally consistent 3D human motion from monocular videos remains challenging under dynamic camera motion. Although SLAM and human mesh recovery (HMR) provide complementary camera and body estimates, directly combining them often leads to inconsistent orientations and accumulated trajectory drift. We present GravHMR, a training-free, plug-and-play framework that couples SLAM and HMR through a shared gravity-aligned reference. By allowing gravity to be estimated independently of the HMR backbone, GravHMR accommodates world-grounded HMR models with or without explicit gravity-view representations. Specifically, Yaw-Aware Orientation Optimization (YAOO) resolves heading inconsistencies by correcting body and velocity orientations about the shared gravity axis. Conditioned on these corrected orientations, Gravity-Aware Trajectory Optimization (GATO) anchors root trajectories in the metric SLAM world by jointly leveraging 2D reprojection, the metric scale implicit in the human body, and the body's own motion. On EMDB-2, GravHMR achieves state-of-the-art performance with 154.0 mm W-MPJPE100 using ViPE and 189.8 mm using masked DROID-SLAM, outperforming TRAM (222.4 mm) under the same masked DROID-SLAM camera estimates. It further reduces W-MPJPE100 by 44.3% over GVHMR (276.5 mm) and by 20.0% over GVHMR + HTD-Refine (192.4 mm) with the same HMR backbone.

papers.title: JEPA-Shield: Safe Diffusion Planning with Latent World Models via Conformal Shielding
papers.abstract: Latent world models enable planning from images, but their predictions do not directly establish whether a robot will satisfy physical constraints. We present JEPA-Shield, which connects a frozen action-conditioned Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) world model to task-space safety enforcement. Two downstream models predict relative motion from imagined latent rollouts and decode unsafe geometry from the current image. Split conformal prediction turns end-to-end motion-prediction errors into multi-horizon uncertainty tubes. A backup-based shield checks these tubes against physical constraints and screens both candidate trajectories and final proposals in diffusion-inspired sampling-based model predictive control. Under the stated exchangeability and initial-backup assumptions, we establish probabilistic constraint satisfaction at action-block boundaries for a returned plan executed without replanning. We also introduce VParkBench, with geometric car and tractor-trailer parking tasks and a editable photorealistic Gaussian-splatting environment. In closed-loop evaluation, JEPA-Shield achieves success rates of 84.4%, 82.3%, and 99.0%, respectively, with no observed constraint violations. Ablations show complementary benefits from shielding and uncertainty calibration. The results demonstrate the importance of grounding latent world-model predictions in task-space quantities and explicitly accounting for prediction uncertainty in safety-critical planning.

papers.title: Think Before You Forecast: Scaling Test-Time Compute for Time Series Forecasting
papers.abstract: Test-time compute has become an important paradigm in computer vision and language modeling, where additional computation at inference time enables models to explore multiple candidate solutions and select or refine the most reliable one. However, time series forecasting models typically produce predictions through a single forward pass, leaving them vulnerable to distribution shifts and non-stationarity that frequently arise in real-world temporal data. We propose Time Test Compute for Time Series (TTC4TS), an architecture-agnostic framework that improves the predictive performance of frozen forecasting models at inference time. Given a pretrained backbone, the generator produces multiple candidate forecast trajectories using augmentation, retrieval, adapter. The synthesizer then selects or combines these candidates using aggregation, classification, or candidate-scoring and ranking methods to produce the final forecast. By increasing the number of candidates, TTC4TS scales test-time compute without retraining the forecasting backbone. Beyond improving point-forecast accuracy, TTC4TS can exploit candidate forecasts for uncertainty quantification, which supports improved interval forecasts. We also theoretically analyze when additional test-time computation improves forecasting. Experiments across diverse datasets and backbones demonstrate consistent gains in accuracy and calibration. Code is provided in https://github.com/Anoise/TTC4TS.

papers.title: Detecting Is Not Choosing: What a World Model Needs to Keep a VLA Policy Safe
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies complete most benchmark tasks but often violate safety constraints. Since they are stochastic, one remedy is to sample several candidate action chunks and execute one that a world model predicts is safe. We ask what such a model must do. In simulation, a lookahead safety filter with the simulator as an exact world model raises the safety rate of three VLA policies on LIBERO and of pi0.5 on LIBERO-Plus by 11.5 to 25.7 points. It also helps pi0.5 on three RoboCasa tasks. Learned critics trained on one policy's data detect dangerous states (pooled AUROC up to 0.864) but rank candidates at one state close to chance (within-decision AUROC 0.551-0.560), and the learned dynamics and video models we test do no better. When the simulator's state is perturbed, selection degrades long before detection. In the loop, a median position error of 3.18 mm removes 70% of the gain on LIBERO-Spatial, partly because the error also corrupts the displacement check. On LIBERO-10 the loss is smaller, and the intervals overlap. The median does not predict the cost: a pixel reader with a 0.56 mm median error keeps 6.5 points less of the gain than Gaussian error of a similar median. A world model for safety should thus be judged by within-state ranking, and its state must be accurate in the tail and on handled objects, not only in the median.

papers.title: Real-Time Kinodynamic Multi-Agent Motion Planning
papers.abstract: Coordinating large robot fleets, from warehouses to quadrotor swarms, requires collision-free trajectories that satisfy dynamic constraints and stay within speed and acceleration bounds. Existing kinodynamic multi-agent planners enforce these bounds during the search or through trajectory optimization after it, which limits fleet size and speed. We present Tickwise Actions to Kinodynamic Trajectories (TAKT), a framework that accounts for the dynamics before the search and reduces planning to a lattice search for double-integrator robots. TAKT analytically bounds the clearance lost when a discrete plan is smoothed and reserves this margin on the lattice. A closed-form convolution provably converts any valid plan into dynamically feasible trajectories with continuous-time collision avoidance. For robots spanning many lattice vertices, we introduce a diamond formulation that permits one-tick sideways yielding and adapt the Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) solvers PIBT and LaCAM to it. With 50 robots, our planners run over 2,000 times faster than the strongest baseline in 2D halls and over 100 times in 3D, with comparable or lower makespan and cost. They plan about a thousand robots in seconds in 2D, and tens of seconds in 3D, and replan up to a thousand robots in real time.

papers.title: Beyond Accuracy: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Hypothesis-Driven Experiment Planning in LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Evaluating large language model (LLM) agents on scientific tasks typically reduces to final-task accuracy, which obscures where reasoning succeeds or breaks down. We introduce a benchmark and diagnostic evaluation framework for hypothesis-driven adaptive experimental planning in closed-world system identification, instantiated in kinetic mechanism identification. The framework goes beyond final accuracy in two ways. First, we evaluate exploration behavior by quantifying the extent to which agents exhibit space-filling or corner-seeking patterns in the experimental design space. Second, we decompose the reasoning process into four interpretable steps: belief update, hypothesis discrimination, discriminative experiment design, and predictive reasoning under interventions, each scored separately on reasoning traces. Across ten LLM agents, we find that stronger agents outperform both adaptive (Bayesian optimization) and non-adaptive (Latin hypercube) baselines and exhibit exploration patterns inconsistent with naive heuristics. Decomposing reasoning reveals that the stronger agents score consistently well across all four steps, whereas weaker agents often succeed at belief update and hypothesis discrimination but are less reliable at translating them into actionable designs and sharp contrastive predictions. Independent expert annotations support predictive reasoning under our stated validation criteria, while evidence for discriminative experiment design is positive but less consistent. The results suggest a gap between recognizing plausible hypotheses and translating them into contrastive predictions, with more tentative evidence for a corresponding experiment-design bottleneck. The benchmark website is available at https://schwallergroup.github.io/beyond-accuracy/.

papers.title: What Test-Time Training Corrects in Latent World Models? A Slow-Fast Approach
papers.abstract: Latent world models plan toward a goal by predicting the outcomes of candidate actions, but under the distribution shift, prediction errors can lead the planner astray. Test-time training using executed actions helps, yet what it corrects and whether its updates should persist across episodes remains unclear. We address both by analyzing the world model's prediction error. On PushObj, an object-pushing task, we probe multiple actions from the same state and decompose the error into an offset shared across actions and an action-dependent component. The offset effectively shifts the planner's goal, and AdaJEPA mainly tracks it: the common shift alone recovers 91% of its planning gain. Part of the offset is episode-specific, so carrying its correction into the next episode does not help and may even hurt. The remaining offset recurs across episodes and action-dependent error can be or needs to be learned and retained from many episodes. Our sft-JEPA therefore uses two learners on different timescales: a fast learner that tracks the offset and resets each episode, and a slow LoRA learner that accumulates recurring knowledge across episodes. Across PushObj, PointMaze, zero-shot planning on RoboCasa (with DINO-WM), and OGBench (with LeWAM), sft-JEPA leads all benchmark averages, improving planning success over AdaJEPA by up to 22 points.

papers.title: ClothCast: Generative Cloth World Modeling under Partial Observability
papers.abstract: World models support robotic manipulation by predicting how the scene evolves under a planned action. For garments this prediction is notoriously difficult: deformations are complex, and self-occlusion leaves much of the cloth unobserved. Planned gripper trajectories provide a useful motion prior because cloth held by a gripper moves with it, while the remaining deformation must be predicted. We introduce ClothCast, a world model that applies this prior to the cloth's points and learns the residual motion. ClothCast takes one RGB-D observation, the camera pose, the robot's own model and the planned gripper trajectories, with no cloth mesh or material parameters. It lifts the observation to a layered point set that includes hypothesized occluded layers, carries the points with a blended rigid prior derived from the gripper poses, and predicts the residual motion with a video-diffusion point-flow model. Over entire 4- to 11-second episodes at 10 Hz, the moved points are rendered into depth, from which a geometry-conditioned completion model synthesizes RGB; after release, a hand-designed settling step replaces the learned motion. We further release ClothCastBench, 10,000 simulated dual-arm cloth-manipulation episodes with the ground-truth cloth mesh, including occluded layers, at every frame. On 492 held-out episodes, ClothCast achieves 2.5x lower sequence-averaged visible-surface Chamfer distance than Flex-π, the strongest baseline in geometry (14.0 mm vs. 35.6 mm), and 3.7 dB higher cloth-region PSNR than Cosmos-Predict2.5, the strongest baseline in cloth PSNR. On a 50-episode ablation subset, the rigid prior alone, applied to ClothCast's learned initial geometry with the same post-processing, already outperforms both geometry-capable baselines, and the learned residual lowers its error by about a third.

papers.title: Graph Neural Networks for Accurate Quasiparticle Energy Levels in Large Supercells of Transition Metal Dichalcogenides
papers.abstract: The GW method is the one of the main workhorses of the materials science community to accurately calculate the electronic bandgap of materials, as it overcomes the gap underestimation problem from Density Functional Theory (DFT). Despite its accuracy, its computational cost becomes prohibitive when calculations have more than 10-100 atoms, which makes more difficult its use for defects, surfaces and moiré systems that demand large supercells. To overcome this problem, we developed a Graph Neural Network trained with smaller GW calculations which can make accurate predictions on large supercells at a small fraction of the computational cost.   Our model uses as features the projection of DFT wavefunctions into localized atomic orbitals, while graph nodes represent the atomic positions and edges represent atom to atom distances, which captures the system geometry. We explore how to do "small AI", providing a workflow of how to create a personal and convenient dataset of GW calculations to train the model that can be applied to different materials so that the final user does not need to rely on massive datasets. We define what must be included in the training dataset to capture the physics of our objective simulation, and perform a Bayesian optimization of hyperparameters. In the case of monolayer MoS$_2$ with a sulfur vacancy our GNN models achieve high accuracy (MAE ranging 10 to 50 meV) with a simplified workflow applicable to other materials, accelerating accurate large electronic structure calculations.

papers.title: Hybrid state-space and attention neural operators for nonlinear structural dynamics under environmental loading
papers.abstract: The computational burden of repeated nonlinear time-history analyses limits their application for structural assessment and design. We therefore propose DeepOJamba, a hybrid neural operator that combines selective state-space recurrence with full attention to predict the structural response history due to dynamic loading. Physical-parameter conditioning and predicted-state transfer between sequences enable a single trained operator to represent varying system conditions and generate response histories beyond its training sequence length. DeepOJamba is evaluated on a 15~MW monopile offshore wind turbine under wind and wave loading. The proposed operator is compared to pure attention, pure state-space, Fourier, and DeepONet operators and is found to give the lowest window error on every channel and the lowest closed-loop fatigue and ultimate-load errors of $9.4\%$ and $6.0\%$, against $14.6\%$ and $8.7\%$ for the next-best pure attention operator examined. Moreover, on sea states outside the training wave band, the error slightly increases by approximately $0.4$ percentage points. Pure state-space operators can approach similar low errors only with a much wider convolution kernel tuned to the tower eigenperiod, which increases the training cost by $40\%$. In all, the results obtained support hybrid neural operators for robust long-duration structural response and demand prediction.

papers.title: RSLaA: Self-Reconfiguring Roadside LiDARs as Agents for 3D Traffic Perception
papers.abstract: Cooperative perception with roadside LiDARs (RSLs) extends the sensing range of autonomous vehicles and resolves onboard-sensor occlusions, particularly at curves and intersections. Because infrastructure deployment is costly, existing work optimizes RSL configurations once, against road geometry and aggregated traffic statistics, and treats them as fixed thereafter. Traffic flow, however, is inherently dynamic, and a placement optimal on average can be far from optimal at any given moment. We introduce RSLaA (Roadside LiDARs as Agents), a framework in which each RSL adaptively adjusts its pose to the evolving traffic scene over decision-time windows. Since ground truth is unavailable at decision time, the framework centers on surrogate metrics computed solely from a probabilistic occupancy grid of historical observations, which predicts the next-window perception performance of candidate poses. We construct a co-simulation benchmark pairing five candidate surrogates with detector-agnostic ground-truth perception labels at every decision window, identifying the multi-view coverage metric J_mv as the most reliable predictor. Upon this validated surrogate we build two adaptive configuration methods, a receding-horizon (MPC) optimizer and a lightweight MAPPO-based multi-agent reinforcement learning scheme with centralized training and decentralized execution. Across 10 sites and 89 six-hour traffic scenarios (890 evaluation runs), adaptive configuration consistently improves the composite perception score over static deployment. Our results indicate that RSLs could be benefitted from being treated as agents.

papers.title: RadioWorld: Transferring World Models to Radio-Frequency Radiance Fields
papers.abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) wave propagation in the physical world constitutes a Radio-Frequency (RF) radiance field, providing rich information for 6G communication and sensing. However, existing neural RF field methods suffer from three fundamental limitations: (1) they predominantly rely on per-scene optimization and cannot generalize to unseen scenes; (2) they require costly reference RF measurements in each target scene; and (3) they degrade severely when extrapolating beyond the vicinity of reference measurements. To overcome these limitations, we present RadioWorld, a general framework that adapts a world model to synthesize RF radiance fields directly from physical scene geometry and transceiver locations, without requiring any reference RF measurements at inference. Specifically, RadioWorld couples two specialized modules within a dual-stream Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architecture: a Scene-Understanding Transformer that encodes 3D scene geometry and transceiver locations to extract environment-aware global EM propagation features, and a Field-Generation Transformer that attends to these features to synthesize the RF radiance field with the local query conditions. We also establish UrbanRF-Bench, a large-scale ray-traced benchmark spanning 657 urban scenes and 32,850 RF radiance fields across seven global cities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RadioWorld significantly outperforms specialized baselines and accurately synthesizes RF fields at arbitrary locations in unseen cities. Code, datasets, and checkpoints will be released upon acceptance.

papers.title: DriveOddsBench: Are Driving Video World Models Aligned with Real-World Odds?
papers.abstract: Video world models predict how a scene will evolve, and their sampled futures are increasingly used in place of the real one, from planning to simulation. These uses assume that the samples are aligned with real-world odds, with each future appearing among them as often as it would follow the same history in reality, yet current evaluations only score how real each sample looks. Testing this assumption on real driving data is hard for three reasons. Each recorded history has only one real future, so the true probabilities are unknown. Physical quantities must be read from video, where reading errors can look like model errors. Finally, the many possible analyses invite selective reporting. We introduce DriveOddsBench, a pre-registered benchmark that addresses all three. First, if the samples follow the real distribution, the rank of the real outcome among them is uniform in every history, so pooled ranks test them without probability labels. Second, one validated instrument reads the same quantities, such as the lead-vehicle gap and the ego motion, from the generated futures and from the real future, which first passes through the world model's autoencoder so that both are read alike. Third, all confirmatory analyses were frozen before any test clip was measured. We test eleven general and driving world models on 200 held-out Argoverse 2 histories in five scenario families, with 35,200 generated futures. None is aligned, and every model underestimates its uncertainty. The real outcome falls outside the range of all 16 samples in 28-61% of cases instead of the 11.8% expected under the real distribution. Five models are significantly skewed, in opposite directions, and the largest errors are in the ego motion. Nine models beat climatology without being aligned, and among these models neither type nor scale predicts which comes closest.

papers.title: NoeVera: Can Knowledge Guide Experiments and Experiments Refine Knowledge?
papers.abstract: With the growing demand for large language model (LLM) services, optimizing LLM serving systems is becoming increasingly complex, and the bottleneck is no longer predicting how a given configuration will perform. The harder problem is deciding what to investigate: which mechanisms matter for a workload, which configurations are worth testing, and what evidence a decision still needs. In this work, we present NoeVera, an agentic Second Brain that goes beyond just one-shot retrieval by turning papers, code, benchmarks, and experimental results into a persistent, provenance-preserving knowledge base with three planes: source evidence, reusable synthesis, and agent memory. Decision-aware retrieval assembles compact evidence packs, role-specific agents reason over them and invoke a simulator (Vidur or GAUSS) whenever quantitative support is needed, and every finding is written back as a scoped evidence record, so knowledge guides experiments and experiments refine knowledge. In configuration search over four serving scenarios, NoeVera comes within 5% of the optimum in a median of 6-7 simulator calls, versus 9 for Bayesian optimization and 15 for a knowledge-free agent with the same tools; on A100 GPUs, its representative configurations deliver ~1.30x vLLM-default throughput and meet every scenario's latency objective. When reused, provenance-preserving evidence records over-generalize on only 8% of applicability traps, versus 28% for a general-purpose agent memory. On the held-out 48-task split of a 72-task benchmark, NoeVera scores 29% higher than an equally equipped agent and 36% higher than its single-call retrieval counterpart (0.80 vs. 0.62 and 0.59), and even when baselines receive NoeVera's own prompts, a statistically significant part of its evidence-evolution advantage remains.

papers.title: DriveTTO: Understanding Search and Selection in Test-Time Trajectory Optimization for End-to-End Driving
papers.abstract: In difficult driving scenes, a learned scorer can select a poor trajectory from a fixed pool even when a better candidate is available. Nearby vehicles and road boundaries can also leave only a narrow range of high-scoring maneuvers. These constraints vary with the scene and are difficult to cover exhaustively during training. We introduce DriveTTO, a training-free method that searches around native proposals and checks each proposed refinement against a retained trajectory. A frozen scorer evaluates completed paths at the endpoints they actually reach, guiding resampling in progressively smaller neighborhoods. From a shared reference, one branch draws on planner proposals and another perturbs vehicle controls. DriveTTO blends their poses at matching times and accepts a branch or fusion update only when both frozen scorers predict a gain. On Navtest, DriveTTO recovers nonzero predictive driver model scores (PDMS) in 51.35% of native zero-score cases on average. Accounting for new failures, the zero-score rate falls from 1.63% to 1.13%. Benchmark-specific configurations achieve 95.54 PDMS and 92.30 extended PDMS (EPDMS) on Navtest, 57.10 EPDMS on Navhard, and 40.1 HD-Score on HUGSIM under observed commands. With a single frozen scorer, DriveTTO-S improves all six evaluated planners on both Navtest and Navhard.

papers.title: FunGrasp-Zero: Field-Conditioned Graph Attention Policy for Zero-Shot Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Functional Grasping
papers.abstract: Dexterous functional grasping is critical for robotic tool use, yet current dexterous hands exhibit substantial morphological diversity. This hardware heterogeneity makes cross-embodiment functional grasping a fundamental but largely unexplored problem. Existing functional grasping methods use retargeted hand poses as guidance, tying task representation to a specific embodiment and failing to explicitly capture object-centric functional contact intent, limiting generalization across hands. To address this, we propose FunGrasp-Zero, a reinforcement learning framework for zero-shot cross-embodiment functional grasping. Instead of relying on embodiment-specific joint configuration, FunGrasp-Zero captures functional intent via an object-centric, cross-embodiment-consistent contact map, adapted to heterogeneous hands through morphological mapping. We construct a hand-object potential field from mapped contact regions, yielding attractive and repulsive guidance vectors. A Field-Conditioned Graph Attention Network (FC-GAT) leverages these vectors to coordinate multi-finger motion across hands, while a potential field reward guides fingers toward target regions and penalizes non-target collisions to enforce functional alignment and stability. We further establish X-FunBench for cross-embodiment functional grasping, evaluating both physical grasp success and functional intent preservation across hands. Evaluated on X-FunBench, our unified policy, co-trained on four embodiments, achieves 86% average grasp success rate across five unseen hands on novel objects. Deployed on four unseen physical hands (Leap, Inspire, Sharpa, Wuji) for novel object grasping, the policy achieves 80% average success rate without fine-tuning. To our knowledge, FunGrasp-Zero is the first RL-based framework to achieve zero-shot cross-embodiment functional grasping across unseen hands in both simulation and the real world.

papers.title: Implementation and Software-in-the-Loop Evaluation of a Trans-Domain Digital Twin Architecture for Autonomous Guidance of the Phoenix VTOL UAV Without Online GNSS
papers.abstract: Autonomous UAV guidance in emergency response, infrastructure monitoring, and cargo transportation requires reliable navigation. However, satellite-based positioning may become unavailable or unreliable in enclosed spaces, blind spots caused by natural obstacles and structures, and environments affected by radio interference and signal spoofing during electronic warfare. This study designs, implements, and evaluates a system based on a Trans-Domain Digital Twin (TDDT) for autonomous guidance of the Phoenix VTOL UAV. Independent navigation, flight dynamics, and meteorological models are coordinated within a cycle of state estimation, prediction, decision-making, command execution, and feedback. Data from inertial, magnetic, pressure, and airspeed sensors, together with environmental information, form the basis for estimation and prediction. Furthermore, a shared state, temporal synchronization, preservation of information provenance, and command traceability establish continuity between models and decisions. The system was tested with a simulated physical twin in a software-in-the-loop environment. Vertical takeoff, movement toward the destination, landing, and autonomous stopping were recorded, and the dynamic model was adjusted to a limited extent based on sensor-derived feedback. Separating the evaluation reference from navigation inputs enabled independent assessment of positioning error and computational performance. The results confirm operational coordination, decision traceability, and closed-loop guidance under the tested conditions, providing a reproducible platform for the development and evaluation of navigation without satellite-based positioning.

papers.title: SilentWAM: Planning in the Masked State of a Diffusion World Model
papers.abstract: World-action models learn from future prediction, but accessing their future representations directly at test time can require costly frame generation. Methods that generate future frames before planning incur additional forward passes, while future co-training methods omit explicit future predictions at inference. We introduce \method, a planner that reads the hidden states of masked future tokens without decoding future frames. We pretrain MMaDA-Parallel-M on driving video using frame-level masked world modeling, which predicts a masked suffix of future frames and explicitly includes inputs with all future frames masked. Learned planning queries attend to these masked positions and the observed context, and a continuous head predicts the trajectory in the same forward pass. With a single front camera, \method reaches 92.0 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 and 89.3 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2, with an end-to-end latency of 60.3\,ms.

papers.title: Your Diffusion-Based Driving Planner Only Needs a Nudge
papers.abstract: Diffusion-based planners capture the multimodality of human driving behavior well, yet covariate shift in closed-loop driving can lead them to generate trajectories that result in collisions or road departures. Reinforcement learning (RL) finetuning offers a promising way to tackle this issue, but applying it to diffusion-based planners is complicated by their iterative denoising process and receding-horizon execution. We find that small adjustments to the planned trajectories can prevent many of these unsafe outcomes. Motivated by this observation, we propose PlanNudge, which preserves the learned planning capabilities of a pretrained diffusion-based planner by freezing it and trains a lightweight policy that we call the nudge policy. At each planning step, the nudge policy outputs a nudge, a two-dimensional adjustment of the speed and curvature of the plan from the frozen planner. The nudge policy is a multilayer perceptron that predicts the nudge in a single forward pass, and both dimensions directly change the motion of the vehicle, so standard off-policy RL can train it in closed-loop simulation. We evaluate PlanNudge on nuPlan, a large-scale autonomous driving benchmark based on real-world driving data. In all six settings, PlanNudge matches or exceeds the final scores of the previous state-of-the-art RL finetuning method while using about one sixth as many environment steps and less than one fifth as much model compute. We also provide guidelines for reward shaping, value learning, and exploration when using off-policy RL to post-train autonomous driving planners. Our results are reported with means and standard deviations over six training runs. Project page: https://zerlinwang.github.io/plannudge/

papers.title: Patterns of wear, fracture, and re-revision in ceramic-on-ceramic total hip arthroplasty: a 31-year retrieval study
papers.abstract: Introduction: Ceramic-on-ceramic (CoC) total hip arthroplasty (THA) is commonly used in younger and more active patients due to its low wear characteristics. However, ceramic fracture and wear-related complications remain important causes of revision. This retrieval study aimed to characterise failure mechanisms and associated patient and implant factors in revised CoC bearings. Methods: A retrospective retrieval analysis of alumina and zirconia-toughened alumina (ZTA) CoC THA bearings revised between 1989 and 2021 was performed. Retrievals were classified as non-fractured primary revisions, fractured primary revisions, or re-revisions. Macroscopic and microscopic assessment of fracture morphology and wear patterns was undertaken. Volumetric wear and radiographic component positioning were assessed in a subset. Associations between ceramic fracture and patient activity, implant characteristics, and head size were analysed using logistic regression. Results: The most common indications for revision were aseptic loosening (35.5%), pain (34.1%), ceramic fracture (17.7%), infection (13.2%), and instability (11.8%). Ceramic fracture predominantly involved the acetabular liner (34 liner fractures versus 12 femoral head fractures). Higher patient activity level was associated with increased odds of fracture (moderate activity: OR 11.8; 95% CI, 2.66–52.7; high activity: OR 5.6; 95% CI, 1.24–25.0). ZTA femoral heads (OR 0.30; 95% CI,0.13–0.66) and larger head sizes were associated with lower odds of fracture ( p < 0.001). Differences in volumetric wear between materials were not significant after adjustment for time in situ . Re-revision cases demonstrated more extensive third-body wear and shorter implant survival. Conclusions: Ceramic fracture in CoC THA most commonly involves the acetabular liner and is associated with patient activity and implant factors. Re-revision cases demonstrate substantial third-body wear and reduced implant survival.

papers.title: An Integrated Experimental‐Numerical Design Framework for Delamination Control in Glass/Epoxy Corrugated Composite Cores
papers.abstract: Delamination in corrugated composite cores is a critical design challenge in lightweight structures, as it can significantly reduce load‐bearing capacity without visible external signs. This study presents an experimental–numerical methodology for investigating delamination in glass/epoxy corrugated cores under mixed‐mode loading. Key cohesive zone model parameters were extracted through double cantilever beam (DCB), end‐notched flexure (ENF), and normal cohesive strength (NCS) tests. A neural network‐based surrogate model was developed as an internal consistency check, recovering these parameters from tensile test data with errors below 1%. Finite element simulations of the DCB and ENF tests, combined with sensitivity analyses, established numerical recommendations, including a maximum element size of 1.0 mm and appropriate initial stiffness ranges. Application to a corrugated core showed that the 2D plane‐strain model captures the three‐phase tensile response with good agreement against experiments. An apparent R‐curve comparison yielded a mean error of 4.8% in key fracture parameters, supporting the model's ability to reproduce progressive toughening. Based on these findings, practical design recommendations are offered regarding corner reinforcement, mesh refinement, and the limitations of simplified analytical models. The proposed methodology provides a reasonable basis for delamination prediction in corrugated composite structures, supported by an internal consistency assessment and systematic sensitivity analyses.

papers.abstract: This article proposes a robust adaptive model-free tracking control (RAMFTC) based on actor-critic reinforcement learning (ACRL) for a linear induction motor (LIM) drive to achieve high-dynamic performance in transportation systems. Owing to the uncertainties, friction forces, parameter disparities, and exterior disturbances that exist in the LIM drive system, the design of a model-based controller cannot achieve this control purpose. The RAMFTC scheme incorporates a model-free integral sliding-mode controller (MF-FOISMC) and a dynamic gains fractional-order extended state observer (DG-FOESO). Furthermore, a radial basis function neural network (RBFNN) via actor-critic reinforcement learning (ACRL) adaptively tune the DG-FOESO parameters and control vector gains is developed. First, a fractional-order integral sliding-mode control (FOISMC) is designed to maintain the LIM drive system stability. In addition, to enhance the robustness and dynamic behavior of the drive system, an adaptive MF-FOISMC is developed, and the total disturbance is estimated using a RL-based DG-FOESO in which robustness of the MF-FOISMC scheme, an adaptive dynamic gain for the observer and the control input gain of the model-free controller are developed through the online adaptation mechanism via RBFNN-based RL. The stability analysis of the proposed RAMFTC is demonstrated by Lyapunov function. The validation results guarantee the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed RAMFTC compared to other control schemes.

papers.title: Endoscopy ergonomics training based on active simulation among gastroenterology fellows: a pilot pre-post study
papers.abstract: Musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) are a major concern for endoscopists. Knowledge and training in endoscopic ergonomics may help prevent them. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a dedicated simulation-based ergonomics training program for gastrointestinal (GI) fellows. A specific ergonomics program combining active learning with theoretical instruction was designed for GI fellows. Practical component was a “spot the difference” in which participants had to identify nine ergonomoc errors. This was followed by a debriefing, a demonstration of correct ergonomic positioning, and a theoretical lecture on ergonomics. Ergonomic knowledge was assessed with the same nine-item questionnaire before the session (T0) and one week (T1) and two months (T2) after it. Eighty-four GI fellows from four university hospitals participated. Most were women (59.5%), the median age was 28.4 years (IQR 27.5–30.5) and 98.8% had never received ergonomic training. Before the session, 26.2% correctly identified the prevalence of endoscopy-related MSDs. Among the 59 fellows who completed the T1, four items improved significantly: MSD prevalence (30.5% to 61.0%, p < 0.001), ideal bed height (71.2% to 91.5%, p = 0.014), ideal screen position (55.9% to 86.4%, p < 0.001), and foot pedal position (39.0% to 62.7%, p = 0.006). Among the 37 fellows who completed T2, three items remained significantly higher than baseline: ideal bed height (59.5% to 83.8%, p = 0.039), ideal screen position (40.5% to 75.7%, p = 0.006), and foot pedal position (32.4% to 62.2%, p = 0.010). Most participating gastroenterology fellows did not correctly identify the prevalence of endoscopy-related MSDs. Participation in a brief simulation-based ergonomics training program was associated with improved performance on an ergonomics knowledge assessment, with evidence of partial retention at 2 months. Controlled studies are needed to determine whether such programs change endoscopic practice and reduce the risk of MSDs.

papers.title: A Study of Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Solving Ordinary and Partial Differential Equations
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have recently emerged as promising alternatives to traditional numerical methods for solving differential equations by directly incorporating governing physical laws into the learning process. However, standard PINNs (std-PINNs) often have difficulty handling nonlinear and stiff partial differential equations (PDEs), particularly in terms of stability and convergence. In this study, we investigate the application of PINNs to solve ordinary differential equations (ODEs) and PDEs, including the damped harmonic oscillator (an ODE), 1D heat equation (a linear PDE), and 1D and 2D Allen–Cahn equations (non-linear PDEs). Std-PINNs are first applied to linear problems to evaluate their baseline performance. To address the limitations of std-PINNs in nonlinear settings, a backward-compatible PINN (bc-PINN) framework is implemented, which decomposes the temporal domain into smaller segments and enforces solution continuity across these segments. The results reveal that std-PINNs achieve high accuracy for simple linear problems but fail to capture the dynamics of nonlinear equations, such as the Allen–Cahn equation. By contrast, bc-PINNs significantly improve prediction accuracy and stability on nonlinear and time-dependent PDEs, successfully approximating complex solution behaviors. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of bc-PINNs as a robust extension of std-PINNs for solving challenging differential equations.

papers.title: Design and Performance Evaluation of Multi - Cavity Synergistic Cooling Structure for Next - Generation Ultra - High Temperature Turbine Blades
papers.abstract: This study presents a systematic investigation of the design, optimization, and performance of the Multi - Cavity Synergistic Cooling (MCSC) structure, a transformative technology tailored for next - generation ultra - high temperature turbine blades. Amid the aviation industry’s pursuit of higher propulsion efficiency and lower emissions, modern turbine inlet temperatures (TITs) have surged to 1900–2000°C—far exceeding the melting limits of nickel - based superalloys (1200–1300°C). MCSC addresses this thermal paradox by integrating impingement, convective, and film cooling into a sequential system that maximizes coolant utilization, breaking the traditional trade - off between cooling effectiveness and coolant consumption. Experimental and numerical analyses confirm that optimized MCSC configurations deliver a 25–30% enhancement in cooling effectiveness, a 15–20% reduction in coolant demand, and a ~100°C drop in maximum blade temperature compared to conventional parallel - flow cooling schemes. These improvements directly support next - generation propulsion goals of boosting overall engine thermal efficiency by 10–15%. Notably, MCSC exhibits strong adaptability to both traditional nickel - based superalloys and emerging ceramic matrix composites (CMCs), expanding its application scope across ground - based turbines and aero - engines. The technology’s practical implementation is enabled by additive manufacturing (e.g., selective laser melting for complex internal channels) and advanced computational optimization (e.g., Kriging - based surrogates, neural network algorithms), while future advancements will focus on integrating adaptive cooling systems and CMCs to unlock stable operation at temperatures exceeding 2000°C.

papers.title: Integrated Seabed Characterization for Offshore Wind Developments: A Perspective on Current Framework, Recent Developments and Future Directions
papers.abstract: Offshore wind energy development represents a critical clean energy strategy, with installations increasingly targeting deeper waters and frontier regions characterized by limited geological precedent and complex subsurface conditions. This experience-based perspective paper describes offshore wind seabed characterization methodology, evaluating traditional survey technologies in the context of recent technological advances—including seismic inversion, machine learning for soil classification, probabilistic frameworks for uncertainty quantification, and synthetic CPT generation—each assessed regarding practical applicability and limitations. Emphasis is placed on risk-managed characterization strategies that iteratively reduce uncertainty using an integrated ground model progressively updated through project phases while accommodating diverse regulatory requirements, environmental considerations, and developer risk tolerances. The paper concludes by identifying four priority areas derived from a workshop on integrated seabed characterization: (1) policy reforms promoting early data acquisition and sharing to reduce development costs; (2) education and workforce development standardizing cross-industry communication; (3) use-inspired research establishing standardized uncertainty quantification methodologies; and (4) fundamental research advancing predictive ground modeling tools. These initiatives collectively address the central challenge of reducing seabed uncertainty to improve offshore wind economics, minimize foundation requirements and material consumption, and reduce installation impacts on marine environments.

papers.title: A New Generative Adversarial Network Deep Learning Model for Displacement Prediction of Deep Foundation Pits
papers.abstract: In order to effectively improve the prediction precision of deep foundation pit displacement and reduce engineering accidents, a set of deep learning models and risk warning methods on the basis of monitoring data was put forward, taking the foundation pit of a coal-unloading storage unit for olefin production project of tail gas comprehensive utilization in Damei-Ganhe Industrial Park of Qinghai Province as an example. Based on the Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) of ARIMA and the CNN-LSTM model, an early-warning model of the displacement safety risk of deep foundation pits was established. Firstly, the Auto Regressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) model was utilized to capture the trend and reduce the noise of the deep foundation pit displacement data. In this model, the long short-term memory (LSTM) network was utilized as the generator, and the convolutional neural network (CNN) model was utilized as the discriminator to choose the generated data close to the distribution of actual data. The smooth Wasserstein distance was utilized as a loss function evaluation method, and the Bayesian optimization method was utilized instead of the grid searching to determine model hyper parameters, so as to realize the process of feature extraction, modelling establishment, parameter optimization, and prediction. The results were compared with those of a feedforward BP network model and Support Vector Machine model. The evaluation results show that for monitoring points C19 and C20, the proposed GAN model based on ARIMA and CNN-LSTM achieves MAPE of 8.540% and 7.202%, and R2 of 0.961 and 0.971, respectively. At the same time, the model is compared with the BP network and SVM model, and it is found that the GAN model based on ARIMA and CNN-LSTM combines the advantages of ARIMA and the CNN-LSTM prediction model, has better prediction effect, and the predicted trend is in accordance with the measured data for the two monitoring points examined. Within the scope of this single case study, the GAN model of ARIMA and CNN-LSTM therefore provides comparatively better prediction performance than the BP and SVM models under identical inputs, and its outputs can be used to derive consistent risk levels for early-warning purposes. The validation of these results covers two monitoring points of one foundation pit project, so the findings do not by themselves ensure structural safety. Further multi-case validations on independent datasets are required before the approach is applied to diverse foundation pit scenarios.

papers.title: Spectral Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Excited Quasinormal Modes of Black Holes
papers.abstract: We investigate the application of the spectral physics-informed neural networks to the computation of black hole quasinormal frequencies (QNFs) with emphasis on the excited modes. Traditional physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) architectures identify the fundamental mode robustly but face significant difficulties for finding the overtones. We explored several regularization strategies to overcome this limitation, and we propose a validation protocol by which we consider a frequency valid only when it appears reproducibly across independent runs. We then use a spectral PINN formulation based on Chebyshev polynomials, in which the only trainable parameters are the complex coefficients of the expansion and the frequency itself. Using an anticollapse term and sigmoid barriers acting on the components of ω, to test the usefulness of the spectral PINNs, we apply the methodology to the Pöschl–Teller potential, to gravitational perturbations of the Schwarzschild black hole, and to the Klein–Gordon field in the dimensionally reduced BTZ black hole. Using a few tens of trainable parameters and requiring no prior knowledge of the frequencies sought, we reproduce six excited frequencies of the first system to machine precision, the first four frequencies of the second, and ten consecutive frequencies of the third. Spectral PINNs are therefore a promising alternative for computing excited QNFs. We identify spectral bias as the main limitation of the method, which points to the need for new strategies able to reach higher excited modes.
